architecture_change: TwoTaskLevel0OneQueryMaskDecoder: two independent query vectors (query_brain, query_lesion) sharing every other weight -- the canvas trunk, all per-level query bridges, all cross-attention update blocks, and the final mask-embedding head. Each training step is either a brain example (CAMRI/Mouse, starts from query_brain, trained against the brain mask) or a lesion example (stroke, starts from query_lesion, trained against the lesion mask), balanced across the epoch, both pushing gradients through the SAME shared weights. This directly tests whether the query-conditioning mechanism does real work: the comparison is this model's brain Dice against outputs/paper_width_level0_decoder (single-task brain-only, no shared weights with anything else) and this model's lesion Dice against outputs/stroke_lesion_only_decoder (single-task lesion-only, likewise no shared weights). If the joint model matches or beats both single-task models, the shared query mechanism is transferring something real between tasks. If it is clearly worse on one or both, the query is just a label at this scale, not a real conditioning mechanism.
